result_summary: A per-DocDistance memo over (doc, source) for the reranker relevance grid and the NLI entailment vector cuts the 55-pair all-pairs sweep of the 11 IBM summaries from 2671.72 s to 266.32 s, 10.03x against a 5x bar, with grounding-grid evaluations falling 110 to 11 exactly as predicted and document embeds 165 to 12. Every emitted byte is unchanged: 73 of 73 pair payloads across four arms are byte-identical to the shipped one-shot distance_wrt_source output, 10 of 10 pairs re-scored through the shipped CLI in a fresh subprocess print the same bytes while covering all 11 documents, V reads 0/24 on the D_sel anchor panel from both arms, and the default-path smd and order_gap values are np.array_equal over the 55 pairs with their metric readings identical off and on. The saving tracks the reusable slot fraction rather than the row count: the anchor-fanout shape reuses only the anchor's grid across ten rows and returns 1.99x, while the no-fanout control where every document appears once records 0 grid hits and +0.22% wall time, the zero-reuse floor the kill gate names. Model-load amortisation is reported separately and is the smaller line: 55 cold CLI invocations extrapolate to 71.6 minutes against 45.0 for the warm loop, 1.59x from the load alone, with the memo adding 9.21x on top.
caveats: Arm timings are a single interleaved off/on pass rather than a median of repeats, because one baseline pass is 45 minutes of INT8 cross-encoder work; off and on run back to back so drift falls on both. The 8.0 load-average ceiling is a foreign-load precondition read once with the notebook idle (4.25); it cannot be enforced between sweeps because this notebook saturates 64 threads, so the between-sweep readings (median 7.20, max 10.75, 3 of 11 above the ceiling after a 60 s settle) are dominated by the notebook's own residual load and are not evidence of foreign contention. The ratio remains platform-dependent. Arm D's baseline is derived from arm A's recorded per-pair times rather than measured a second time, so its 1.99x is a derived figure; its memo pass is measured. Byte-identity against the shipped command itself is direct for 10 of 55 pairs, chosen to cover all 11 documents; the other 45 are diffed against the shipped in-process DocDistance.distance_wrt_source payload, which is the strongest available comparison while --pairs is unbuilt. The cold-CLI line extrapolates 55 invocations from 10 measured runs (median 78.09 s) rather than paying for all 55. The kill gate counts the campaign's registered fixture specifications, since no production sweep specification exists in the repository, so it cannot fail on the registered fixture by construction; the two zero-repeat controls show the shape that would kill it. The grid cache is unbounded in the number of distinct documents per instance and its memory was not measured; a grid is n_doc x n_source floats, larger than an embedding row, so a shipping memo needs a size bound. Cached arrays are handed back by reference, not copied, so a caller that mutated them would corrupt later hits; nothing in the shipped path does. Nothing under src/ was changed and the --pairs option on distance-wrt-source is not built here, the batch loop was driven in-process, so acting on this verdict means building both halves of the registered lever in a follow-up.
